launches.title: HyperBench - AI agents for hardware/software co-development
launches.body:
Hyperbench is an agentic engineering platform for hardware and software co-development.

Coding agents often lack the context to understand how a software change affects a physical system. Hyperbench maps repositories, hardware components, interfaces, protocols, and test evidence into one system graph, giving agents the context to understand how the pieces connect.

Agents use that graph to trace failures across components, delegate repairs across repositories, and test their changes on real hardware (hardware-in-the-loop). In a system-level reasoning benchmark, Hyperbench scored 20% higher in correctness and reduction in debugging speed compared with vanilla Claude and Codex.

We’re are Stanford CS & Physics engineers that bring experience from Anduril and OpenAI . We saw how separate hardware and software workflows made integration failures difficult to trace, and are building Hyperbench to bring system context, agent development, and hardware testing into one environment.
